**Thursday, September 3, 2026 -**_** ** Iran launches attacks on U.S. bases in
Kuwait and UAE. Latest wave of U.S. strikes on Iran kill 18, injure 142. Iran
seizes ship in the Gulf, arrests crew members. U.S. President Donald Trump
says Iran bombing won't last "too long," suggests naming Strait of Hormuz
after himself. Trump aides reportedly pushing to quiet Iran war until November
midterms. Iranian rial hits record low. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin
Netanyahu says Israel's mission in Iran "not yet finished." U.S. Secretary of
State Marco Rubio warns other countries not to aid Iran, threatens sanctions.
Iran criticizes UNICEF over lack of response to deaths of Iranian children.
Six vessels transited Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday. Israeli forces kill two
Palestinians in northern Gaza. Israel kills two Palestinian teenagers in the
occupied West Bank. Israel establishes three new settlements in a week as
demolitions, arrests continue across occupied West Bank. Israeli Defense
Minister Israel Katz: Removing Palestinians from Gaza remains the "only
solution." EU foreign ministers split over Israel trade sanctions amid West
Bank settler violence. Yemen's Saudi-backed forces say Ansarallah fired 14
missiles as heavy fighting erupts in Taiz. Israeli forces carry out large
explosions across southern Lebanon despite "ceasefire." Israel agrees to
release five Lebanese detainees as forces detain three others in southern
Lebanon. Save the Children: Israel killing average of seven children daily in
Lebanon since March. Trump administration backs OpenAI in copyright fight
against New York Times. Federal judge blocks Trump's latest birthright
citizenship order. House rejects GOP amendment to lock Supreme Court at nine
seats. New York City schools ban AI tools, cap screen time for elementary,
middle schoolers. ICE preparing $5 million contract to build national voter
database. Whistleblower says ICE skipped background checks in rush to hire
recruits. Widow of U.S. airman killed in Iran war claims she was denied
benefits. Deposed Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro asks U.S. judge to
dismiss drug trafficking charges. Malta jury acquits businessman of
masterminding 2017 murder of journalist. Australia, U.S. to expand defense
ties. UN report finds foreign networks fueling Sudan drone warfare. U.S. to
use Organization of American States to isolate Nicaragua over constitutional
changes. Honduran court drops charges against former President. Norway seizes
Russian ship in support of Ukrainian energy firm._

**This is Drop Site Daily, our free news recap We send it Monday - Friday**

* * *

# Iran

  * **Iran launches attacks on U.S. bases in Kuwait and UAE:** Iran's army [said](https://www.tasnimnews.ir/en/news/2026/09/03/3687717/iran-army-attacks-target-us-communications-systems-hangars-in-kuwait-uae) it launched missile and drone attacks early Thursday targeting U.S. military facilities in Kuwait and the United Arab Emirates, including the Ahmed Al-Jaber Air Base in Kuwait and Al-Minhad Air Base in the UAE, Iran's Tasnim News Agency reported.

    * Kuwait was [defending](https://x.com/DropSiteNews/status/2095339905031295119) itself from Iranian attacks, the Kuwaiti army [announced](https://x.com/kuwaitarmyghq/status/2095324773253341615?s=46) on X, adding that any explosions heard were a result of their air defenses responding to "hostile" missile and drone attacks.

  * **Latest wave of U.S. strikes on Iran kill 18, injure 142:** The U.S strikes on Iran on Tuesday and Wednesday killed at least 18 Iranians and injured 142, according to a spokesperson for the Iranian health ministry. The ministry noted that 61 of the wounded were women and 44 were under the age of 18.

    * Six members of Iran's navy were killed in U.S. strikes on Tuesday, the Tasnim news agency reported on Thursday, without specifying where they were killed.

  * **Iran seizes ship in the Gulf, arrests crew members:** Iranian ⁠border ⁠guards seized a vessel carrying 382,000 liters (101,000 gallons) ⁠of "smuggled fuel" in the northern ⁠Gulf, Iranian state media reported on Tuesday, adding that the guards also arrested 11 of the ship's crew members.

  * **Trump says Iran bombing won 't last "too long," suggests naming Strait of Hormuz after himself: **U.S. President Donald Trump told reporters in the Oval Office on Wednesday that the renewed U.S. bombing campaign against Iran would not continue for "too long," but said the U.S. was "prepared to do another" attack at "any time we want."

    * In the same remarks, he claimed again that the U.S. was in control of the Strait of Hormuz, and that the U.S. is "bringing lots of boats out every day with millions of barrels of oil" through the Strait daily. "We are, for the most part, doing it without trouble. Every once in a while they shoot a drone, and we knock it down," he added.

    * On Truth Social, Trump suggested he would attempt to change the name of the passageway to "TRUMP STRAIT," following similar unilateral name changes of the Gulf of Mexico and Lake Ontario.

  * **Trump aides reportedly pushing to quiet Iran war until November midterms:** Trump's senior aides are [pushing](https://www.reuters.com/world/trump-aides-fearing-midterm-rout-push-keep-iran-war-quiet-now-2026-09-02/) to prevent an escalation in the ongoing war in Iran before the November congressional midterm elections, hoping to limit Republican losses, Reuters reported.

    * Sources told the outlet that White House officials may consider ramping up military action after the elections, though officials do not presently think there is a risk of a return to full-scale war.

    * The war is unpopular with voters, with 63% of Americans disapproving of the conflict and only 31% approving, according to a late August Reuters/Ipsos poll.

    * Trump responded to these and similar reports on Wednesday, claiming he was "not affected by the election" because he himself was not running.

  * **Iranian rial hits record low:** The Iranian currency dropped to a record low of more than 2.2 million rials to one U.S. dollar on Wednesday, Reuters reported.

  * **Netanyahu says Israel 's mission in Iran "not yet finished": **Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu [said](https://www.middleeasteye.net/live-blog/live-blog-update/netanyahu-israels-mission-iran-not-yet-finished) that his country's mission in Iran was "not yet finished" in remarks to i24News on Wednesday, saying that "all of our systems" remained committed to "bringing down" the Iranian government.

    * President Donald Trump told the Israeli news outlet Kan on Wednesday that Israel does not need to worry about a resumption of the war with Iran, claiming that he would "take care of it."

  * **Rubio warns other countries not to aid Iran, threatens sanctions** : U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio warned that any country helping Iran create "mechanisms" to generate funds would also face American sanctions.

    * He added, in remarks to reporters, that "nothing that anyone is providing Iran is in any way impeding our ability to act as necessary to protect the United States."

    * Rubio also said that the Strait of Hormuz would "remain open" and that the U.S would "continue to target" entities in the state that pose a threat to its interests.

  * **Iran criticises UNICEF over lack of response to deaths of Iranian children:** At a UNICEF board meeting in New York on Wednesday, Amir Saeid Iravani, Iran's representative to the United Nations, criticized the children's rights agency for what Tehran described as its failure to condemn attacks by the United States and Israel that have killed Iranian children.

    * UNICEF has previously expressed concern over child casualties in Iran and called on all parties to comply with international humanitarian law, but has generally not attributed individual attacks to the U.S. or Israel.

  * **Six vessels transited Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday:** Just six ships transited the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday, down from 11 on Tuesday, according to the latest data from Kpler, reported on by Reuters.

    * The vessels included two very large gas carriers, two long-range tankers, one Supramax tanker and one Panamax tanker, according to the firm.

    * The number may be updated, with ships that switch off their transponders possibly being added to the tally.

# Palestine

  * **Israeli forces kill two Palestinians, including child, in northern Gaza:** Two Palestinians, including a child, were [killed](https://www.wafa.ps/news/2026/9/3/%D8%B4%D9%87%D9%8A%D8%AF%D8%A7%D9%86-%D8%A8%D9%8A%D9%86%D9%87%D9%85%D8%A7-%D8%B7%D9%81%D9%84-%D9%88%D9%85%D8%B5%D8%A7%D8%A8%D9%88%D9%86-%D8%A8%D8%B1%D8%B5%D8%A7%D8%B5-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A7%D8%AD%D8%AA%D9%84%D8%A7%D9%84-%D9%81%D9%8A-%D8%A8%D9%8A%D8%AA-%D9%84%D8%A7%D9%87%D9%8A%D8%A7-%D8%B4%D9%85%D8%A7%D9%84-%D9%82%D8%B7%D8%A7%D8%B9-%D8%BA%D8%B2%D8%A9-153307) and several others wounded by Israeli forces gunfire in Beit Lahia, northern Gaza, on Thursday, WAFA reported.

    * On Wednesday, an Israeli strike on a tent in Al-Mawasi, southern Gaza, wounded five, with one man later dying from wounds sustained in the attack.

  * **Israel kills two Palestinian teenagers in the occupied West Bank:** Israeli gunfire killed Khalil Abu Alia, 16, and Omar Mohammed Naasan, 19, as soldiers and settlers raided al-Mughayyir, northeast of Ramallah in the occupied West Bank on Wednesday. Khalil's uncle, Mohammed Hussein Abu Aliya, spoke to Drop Site contributor Mutasem Sqf ElHait as the attack continued. He described homes raided, sheep taken and residents abused: "Children, women, young men, even people passing by on the road. No one was spared."

    * Israel's military said it fired at "key instigators with the aim of removing the threat" and accused Palestinians of throwing rocks when soldiers took livestock it claimed belonged to Israelis. "Hits were observed," its statement said.

    * "The machinery of beatings, destruction, snipers, and terror is operating 24 hours a day," Abu Aliya said. "Our children are dear and precious to us. They love life. They love a dignified life."

    * **Watch the dispatch by Mutasem Sqf ElHait[ here](https://x.com/DropSiteNews/status/2095281611126214815).**

  * **Israel establishes three new settlements in a week as demolitions, arrests continue across occupied West Bank:**

    * **Tubas:** Palestinian authorities [received](https://www.wafa.ps/news/2026/9/3/%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%B4%D8%A4%D9%88%D9%86-%D8%A7%D9%84%D9%85%D8%AF%D9%86%D9%8A%D8%A9-%D8%A7%D8%B3%D8%AA%D9%84%D8%A7%D9%85-%D8%AC%D8%AB%D9%85%D8%A7%D9%86-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%B4%D9%87%D9%8A%D8%AF-%D8%AC%D8%A7%D8%AF-%D8%A7%D9%84%D9%84%D9%87-%D8%AC%D8%A7%D8%AF-%D8%A7%D9%84%D9%84%D9%87-%D8%A8%D8%B9%D8%AF-%D8%A7%D8%AD%D8%AA%D8%AC%D8%A7%D8%B2%D9%87-%D9%85%D9%86%D8%B0-%D8%AA%D8%B4%D8%B1%D9%8A%D9%86-153317) the body of Jadallah Jihad Juma Jadallah, a boy from Far'a refugee camp, after Israeli authorities had withheld his body since his killing on November 16, 2025, WAFA reported. Israel continues to withhold 799 documented Palestinian bodies, including those of 80 children.

    * **Hebron:** Israeli forces detained a Palestinian man from Susya in Masafer Yatta on Thursday, as settlers released livestock onto Palestinian land and around homes. On Wednesday, Israeli forces [demolished](https://www.wafa.ps/news/2026/9/3/%D9%87%D8%AF%D9%85-38-%D9%85%D9%86%D8%B4%D8%A3%D8%A9-%D9%88%D8%AA%D8%B4%D8%B1%D9%8A%D8%AF-58-%D9%85%D9%88%D8%A7%D8%B7%D9%86%D8%A7-%D9%81%D9%8A-%D9%85%D8%B3%D8%A7%D9%81%D8%B1-%D9%8A%D8%B7%D8%A7-%D9%8A%D8%B9%D8%B2%D8%B2%D8%A7%D9%86-%D9%85%D8%AE%D8%B7%D8%B7-%D8%B6%D9%85-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%B6%D9%81%D8%A9-153287) 38 residential, agricultural, and service structures in al-Tabban, Masafer Yatta, displacing eight Palestinian families comprising 58 people, including 26 children and 30 women.

    * **Bethlehem/Hebron:** Israeli authorities [established](https://www.wafa.ps/news/2026/9/3/%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A7%D8%AD%D8%AA%D9%84%D8%A7%D9%84-%D9%8A%D9%81%D8%AA%D8%AA%D8%AD-%D9%85%D8%B3%D8%AA%D8%B9%D9%85%D8%B1%D8%A9-%D8%AC%D8%AF%D9%8A%D8%AF%D8%A9-%D8%B6%D9%85%D9%86-%D9%83%D8%AA%D9%84%D8%A9-%D8%BA%D9%88%D8%B4-%D8%B9%D8%AA%D8%B5%D9%8A%D9%88%D9%86-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A7%D8%B3%D8%AA%D9%8A%D8%B7%D8%A7%D9%86%D9%8A%D8%A9-%D8%AC%D9%86%D9%88%D8%A8-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%B6%D9%81%D8%A9-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%BA%D8%B1%D8%A8%D9%8A%D8%A9-153290) a new settlement in the Gush Etzion bloc on Wednesday, the third new settlement within a week. The settlement was established on an axis connecting the bloc's western and eastern sections, with its regional council saying it was intended to create territorial continuity between them. Two other settlements were established on Monday: Makida/Doran, northwest of Hebron, and Noa, southeast of Jenin.

    * **Jenin/Tubas/Tulkarm:** The Israeli military announced a "military exercise" in the cities of Jenin, Tubas, and Tulkarm "starting from the morning hours until noon."

    * **East Jerusalem:** Israeli forces [detained](https://www.facebook.com/reel/2100203904186602/) several employees of the Hizma municipality, northeast of occupied East Jerusalem, during a raid on the town on Thursday and seized a municipal vehicle, according to the Jerusalem Governorate.

  * **Israel 's Katz: Removing Palestinians from Gaza remains the "only solution":** Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz [said](https://x.com/dropsitenews/status/2095248764781076592?s=46) Israel remains prepared to forcibly remove Palestinians from Gaza "by sea, by air, by every way possible," describing the ethnic cleansing of the Strip as the "only solution." Katz said Trump has not canceled the plan but "froze it" after pressure from Arab governments, while countries willing to receive Palestinians want U.S. backing. He added Israel expects a future "green light" to advance militarily and territorially if Hamas is deemed to have violated its commitments.

    * One of Trump's two main Gaza advisers, Jared Kushner, made a similar threat after meeting Netanyahu last month, saying that if Hamas failed to decommission its weapons, the U.S. would back Israel resuming the war to "finish the job."

  * **EU foreign ministers split over Israel trade sanctions amid West Bank settler violence:** Ireland and Spain, backed by Belgium and the Netherlands, [pushed](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/9/3/eu-remains-divided-over-trade-sanctions-on-illegal-israeli-settlements) EU foreign ministers to back trade restrictions on goods from illegal Israeli settlements at an informal Gymnich meeting hosted by Ireland in Wicklow on Tuesday and Wednesday, Al Jazeera reported. Germany, Austria, Czechia, and Hungary opposed the move, warning it would damage the body's diplomatic ties with Israel.

    * Irish Foreign Minister Helen McEntee said the bloc should act "collectively" on international law, but the body's foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas did not address sanctions at the post-meeting press conference.

    * It remains unclear whether such restrictions would need unanimous approval or a simple majority.

# Yemen

  * **Yemen 's Saudi-backed forces say Ansarallah fired 14 missiles as heavy fighting erupts in Taiz: **The Saudi-backed government said Ansarallah forces fired 14 ballistic missiles and launched drones at populated areas in Taiz and Hodeidah governorates, as heavy fighting continued on the Al-Kadaha front southwest of Taiz city.

    * The military's media center claimed air defences shot down several drones over Taiz and the western coast, while government forces "neutralised sources of threats and hostile fire" in the Al-Kadaha sector.

    * The media center also released footage purporting to show government strikes on Ansarallah fighters and positions in Marib and Al Bayda governorates, without specifying when the attacks took place.

# Lebanon

  * **Israeli forces carry out large explosions across southern Lebanon despite "ceasefire": **Israeli forces carried out a series of large explosions in several towns in southern Lebanon on Thursday, according to Lebanon's National News Agency.

    * A massive [explosion](https://www.nna-leb.gov.lb/ar/news/561067/%D8%AA%D9%81%D8%AC%D9%8A%D8%B1-%D8%A5%D8%B3%D8%B1%D8%A7%D8%A6%D9%8A%D9%84%D9%8A-%D8%B6%D8%AE%D9%85-%D9%81%D9%8A-%D9%83%D9%81%D8%B1%D8%AA%D8%A8%D9%86%D9%8A%D8%AA-%D8%A3%D8%AD%D8%AF%D8%AB-%D8%AF%D9%88%D9%8A%D8%A7%D9%8B-%D9%87%D8%A7%D8%A6%D9%84%D8%A7%D9%8B-2) in Kfar Tebnit, Nabatieh, sent thick clouds of smoke into the air and was heard across large parts of southern Lebanon.

    * In the Marjayoun district, Israeli forces [carried out](https://www.nna-leb.gov.lb/ar/news/561044/%D8%AB%D9%84%D8%A7%D8%AB%D8%A9-%D8%AA%D9%81%D8%AC%D9%8A%D8%B1%D8%A7%D8%AA-%D9%81%D9%8A-%D8%A8%D9%84%D8%AF%D8%A9-%D8%A8%D9%86%D9%8A-%D8%AD%D9%8A%D8%A7%D9%86-2) three explosions in Bani Hayyan, as well as explosions in Qantara.

    * Forces also conducted detonations in the towns of Haddatha and Baraachit in the Bint Jbeil district.

  * **Israel agrees to release five Lebanese detainees as forces detain three others in southern Lebanon:** Israel [agreed](https://www.timesofisrael.com/liveblog_entry/pms-office-confirms-israel-freeing-5-lebanese-civilian-detainees-as-beirut-aids-search-for-jewish-remains/) to release five Lebanese detainees as part of negotiations with Lebanon, in return for Beirut's assistance in efforts to locate and return the remains of figures from Lebanon's Jewish community, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's office said on Thursday, according to The Times of Israel. The office acknowledged the five were civilians and that there was "no reason to continue holding them in Israel."

    * The International Committee of the Red Cross [completed](https://www.nna-leb.gov.lb/ar/news/561070/%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%AC%D9%8A%D8%B4-%D8%AA%D8%B3%D9%84%D9%91%D9%85-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A3%D8%B3%D9%8A%D8%B1-%D9%85%D8%A7%D9%84%D9%83-%D8%BA%D8%A7%D8%B2%D9%8A-%D8%B9%D8%A8%D8%B1-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%B5%D9%84%D9%8A%D8%A8-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A3%D8%AD%D9%85%D8%B1-%D8%B9%D9%86%D8%AF-%D9%85%D8%B9%D8%A8%D8%B1-%D8%A7%D9%84%D9%86%D8%A7%D9%82%D9%88%D8%B1%D8%A9-2) the first handover, with the Lebanese army receiving Malek Ghazi at the Naqoura crossing, Lebanon's NNA reported.

    * Separately, Israeli forces [raided](https://www.nna-leb.gov.lb/ar/news/561068/%D9%82%D9%88%D8%A9-%D8%A5%D8%B3%D8%B1%D8%A7%D8%A6%D9%8A%D9%84%D9%8A%D8%A9-%D8%AA%D8%AA%D9%88%D8%BA%D9%84-%D9%81%D9%8A-%D8%AD%D9%84%D8%AA%D8%A7-%D9%88%D8%AA%D8%B9%D8%AA%D9%82%D9%84-%D8%AB%D9%84%D8%A7%D8%AB%D8%A9-%D9%85%D9%86-%D8%A3%D8%A8%D9%86%D8%A7%D8%A1-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A8%D9%84%D8%AF%D8%A9-2) Halta in Hasbaya District on Thursday morning, surrounded several homes and prevented residents from leaving before detaining three men and withdrawing, according to NNA.

  * **Save the Children: Israel killing average of seven children daily in Lebanon since March** : Israel has [killed](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/9/2/israel-kills-or-injures-7-children-a-day-in-lebanon-invasion-report-says) an average of seven children per day in Lebanon since March despite agreements aimed at ending the fighting, Save the Children said Wednesday.

    * The report noted the risk fighting has posed to education in the country, with 340 schools damaged or destroyed, according to the latest survey by the Lebanese Ministry of Education.

    * Israel has killed at least 4,300 people in the country, including 257 children, wounded over 12,000, and destroyed 60 to 70 villages over the past six months. More than 348,800 people remain displaced in the country despite a June ceasefire, according to the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs.

# U.S. News

  * **Trump administration backs OpenAI in copyright fight against New York Times:** In the legal fight between OpenAI and The New York Times, the Justice Department filed court papers Tuesday supporting the artificial intelligence firm's argument that training its AI models on internet content, including news articles, is protected under copyright law's "fair use" doctrine.

    * The department wrote that "the creative possibilities and public benefits" of training large language models on such content "far outweigh any competitive harm."

    * The Times, which sued OpenAI in 2023, has alleged the company effectively stole billions of dollars' worth of its journalism. It criticized the administration's position in a statement Tuesday, accusing the DOJ of "siding with a handful of trillion-dollar AI companies at the expense of the countless American creators whose work they stole."

  * **Federal judge blocks Trump 's latest birthright citizenship order: **U.S. District Judge **Deborah Boardman** [issued](https://www.politico.com/news/2026/09/02/birthright-citizenship-order-ruling) a preliminary injunction Wednesday barring enforcement of President Donald Trump's latest executive order on birthright citizenship, saying the order defies the Supreme Court's June ruling striking down a previous attempt to end birthright citizenship entirely.

    * The order seeks to deny citizenship to children born on U.S. soil to parents who entered through a "commercial transaction" or are classified as "alien enemies."

  * **House rejects GOP amendment to lock Supreme Court at nine seats** : The House [voted](https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/congress/house-democrats-block-constitutional-amendment-supreme-court-justices-rcna595736) down 212-206 a proposed constitutional amendment offered by Rep. **Andy Biggs** to permanently fix the number of Supreme Court justices at nine.

    * The measure was part of a broader series of GOP messaging votes during the Congress's new session, which included a resolution denouncing socialism, which passed on Tuesday.

    * Support for expanding the court has grown within the Democratic mainstream in recent years, with Rep. **Jim Clyburn** recently endorsing 13 seats and former Vice President **Kamala Harris** voicing support for expansion this summer, following the conservative majority's rulings on abortion, voting rights, and presidential immunity.

  * **NYC schools ban AI tools, cap screen time for elementary, middle schoolers** : New York City Mayor **Zohran Mamdani** and Schools Chancellor **Kamar Samuels** [announced](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-09-02/nyc-public-schools-ban-ai-for-students-restrict-screen-time) a policy banning generative AI tools for preschool through 8th grade students and prohibiting companion chatbots for all grades. The change will apply to roughly 600,000 public school students starting September 10.

    * The policy also caps screen time on personal devices, recommending 30 minutes daily for grades 3-5 and 45 minutes for grades 6-8.

    * "The tech industry wants us to believe that AI-powered early education is not only inevitable, but necessary. We do not see it that way," Mamdani said.

    * There are more than 80 active campaigns in 24 states to amend policies related to screen use and classroom devices.

  * **ICE preparing $5 million contract to build national voter database** : Immigration and Customs Enforcement is preparing to [award](https://www.wired.com/story/ice-plans-to-pay-5-million-to-create-national-voting-database/) a contract worth up to $5 million to a company that will build a national database of voter registration and voting history files, Wired reported.

    * A federal document published last week notes that the contractor will need to obtain data from all 50 states on its population's voting history for every federal election--including general, primary, runoff, and special elections--and voter registration information, which experts believe will impinge upon U.S. voters' right to privacy.

    * The effort is part of a broader push by DHS and the Trump administration to scrutinize voter rolls ahead of the midterms, including a $125 million contract with Thomson Reuters for access to its CLEAR database, ICE's acquisition of voter rolls from counties in Texas and North Carolina, and a new surge in election fraud investigations led by DHS, despite minimal evidence of noncitizen voting.

  * **Whistleblower says ICE skipped background checks in rush to hire recruits** : A former ICE unit chief who oversaw vetting for more than 100 employees [filed](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/09/03/us/ice-recruits-national-security-risk-whistleblower.html) a whistleblower complaint alleging the agency fast-tracked "improperly vetted" recruits during a 2025 hiring surge, skipping fingerprint, identity, and credit checks before extending job offers, according to The New York Times.

    * After filing his complaint, the whistleblower was interrogated for four hours by agency lawyers, had his laptop seized, and was placed on leave for 10 months over unspecified "serious misconduct" allegations before being reinstated without findings of wrongdoing and retiring in July.

  * **Pentagon pulls classified war planning documents after report on generals ' Iran war concerns:** The Pentagon [removed](https://www.washingtonpost.com/national-security/2026/09/02/pentagon-cuts-access-classified-information-amid-iran-war-concerns/) decades of classified documents associated with the Secretary of Defense Orders Book from an internal SIPRNet web portal after The Washington Post reported that senior military officers had raised objections to prolonged operations against Iran.

    * Several generals had "non-concurred" with extending large-scale operations against Iran, according to the Post, warning it was unsustainable and risked weakening the military's ability to confront threats elsewhere.

    * A former defense official said restricting access to the document, which details ship, unit, and weapons availability, may complicate time-sensitive logistical decisions for the military, whose commanders rely on the document, and fewer of whom will now have direct access to it.
